yzoh9l:204: Progress status is written to two carriers simultaneously—a human-readable scannable terminal summary (numbers, ratios, anomalies) and a structured state file for the Agent to read (task ID, status, output path, failure reason). The deep logic behind this design is: humans need an intuitive sense of "where are we now" when recovering; the Agent needs precise instructions on "where to continue" when recovering, and the two data structures are completely heterogeneous. Forcibly merging them not only creates redundancy but also increases noise for Agent parsing. Many teams implement persistence but overlook the dual-channel design, which is a common hidden cause of long-horizon task recovery failure.
